title: Capacity Margin Exchange — playbook and scenario slate
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for converting short-term capacity constraints into controlled margin changes (and vice versa). Idea: treat capacity (reserved GPU hours, burst credits) as an asset we can trade against price and headcount levers to stabilize runway and SLA commitments for Q1–Q3 2027.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- When spot GPU pressure or headcount gaps threaten throughput, we can either: (A) buy temporary capacity (burst), (B) nudge prices / quotas, or (C) reallocate headcount from lower-impact work.
- This doc defines 3 portfolio scenarios (Soft, Moderate, Hard), quantifies margin delta per action, and gives an operational runbook with owners and comms templates.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline monthly hosted API token volume: 120B tokens. Avg unit margin (hosted mix): $0.0009 per token.
- Dedicated commitments: 18% of revenue, steady. Bursting options available at +35% on top of reserved rates.
- Peak-day capacity surge episodes historically last 3–7 days and consume 12–22% additional GPU hours vs steady-state.
- Average hiring lead time for infra/SRE/ops engineers: 9–12 weeks.

Scenario slate (headline numbers):
1) Soft noise (1–2 short surges per quarter): absorb via cache tuning + small burst credits. Expected margin erosion: ~0.5–0.9 p.p. over quarter. Headcount impact: none.
2) Moderate pressure (sustained 4–6% monthly growth, spot volatility): use targeted price nudges for high-consumption customers + 2–4k GPU-hour burst buy. Margin erosion: ~1.5–3.0 p.p. if we solely buy capacity, or ~0.2–1.0 p.p. if combined with 3–5% price nudges for top 5% customers. Headcount impact: re-align 2 FTEs from product infra to ops for 8 weeks.
3) Hard shock (demand + supply crunch): immediate 20–35% additional capacity need. Options: large short-term pricing tiers, staged throttles, or emergency hires/contractors. Margin effect: +5–12 p.p. downside if capacity bought at premium, or +2–6 p.p. downside if we enact steep pricing steps for non-enterprise segments. Headcount: hire/contract 4–6 infra SREs or accept reduced SLA to enterprise customers.

Numeric worked example (Moderate pressure):
- Incremental GPU hours needed: 30k GPU-hours in month. Market spot premium: $3.20 / GPU-hour above reserved. Incremental cost: $96k.
- Revenue at-risk (top 10 customers meter at heavy token mix): $300k for month. If we enact a 3% price uplift on top-100 accounts (approx $250k incremental revenue) netting $154k after churn assumptions.
- Net margin delta: if we choose burst purchase only -> -$96k / month (approx -0.6 p.p. on run-rate margin). If we combine burst + 3% targeted uplift -> break-even to +$58k improvement depending on churn.

Headcount phasing and reallocation guide:
- Short-term: redeploy 2 infra engineers from feature backlog to burst-onboarding + cache tuning for 6–8 weeks. Expected throughput gain: 6–12% reduction in per-token GPU-hours.
- Medium-term (3–6 months): prioritize hiring 2 SRE contractors for capacity automation; convert to full-time if sustained demand.
- Long-term (6–12 months): invest in quantization/compilation work (applied-ml + serving-runtime) to reduce marginal GPU cost by target 8–15%.

Pricing levers (ordered by customer impact):
1) Top-customers targeted uplift (1–5%): low friction for enterprise with contract negotiation. Use credits & grandfathering windows.
2) Consumption tiers for hosted API: introduce a burst surcharge band (applies after 95th percentile daily usage).
3) Time-of-day pricing windows for non-SLA workloads (internal pilot).
4) Quota enforcement & optional throttles for older API versions.

Operational runbook (who does what):
- Finance (owner: Elena Park): models scenario P&L, signs off on price uplift bands, prepares customer impact decks.
- Sales & AE (owner: Kiran Shah): run targeted outreach for proposed uplifts, coordinate grandfathering, track churn risk.
- Product (owner: Sophie Le): scope rollback/backstop features; enable per-customer billing gates and rate limits.
- Serving runtime / Infra (owner: Miguel Rivera): implement burst routing, enable quick KV cache policy tuning, monitor GPU-hour burn.
- SRE (owner: Tom Brody): on-call operational lead during surge; execute capacity flip to reserved pools.

Communication templates (short):
- Internal alert subject: "Capacity Margin Exchange — ACTIVATE [Soft|Moderate|Hard]"
  Body: summary of trigger, recommended action, owners, expected margin impact, timeframe, and customer teams to brief.

- Customer outreach snippet (for targeted uplift):
  "Dear <AE>, we are seeing persistent changes in workload cost profiles. To maintain performance SLAs we are proposing a small consumption-tier adjustment for high-consumption usage. We will offer a 60d grandfather window and optional burst credits — happy to review specific usage patterns."

Trigger thresholds (operational):
- Soft: 7-day rolling GPU-hour burn > 1.15x baseline AND cache hit rate < 88% -> activate cache tune + small burst.
- Moderate: 7-day rolling GPU-hour burn > 1.35x baseline OR top-10 customers account for > 46% of net surge -> activate targeted uplifts + 24–72h burst commit.
- Hard: spot market premium > 1.5x reserved AND 7-day burn > 1.6x baseline -> recommend emergency pricing band + request exec sign-off for capacity buy.

Checklist prior to price/quota changes:
- Finance: model 3 sensitivity points (0%, +3%, +6% uplift) including churn assumptions.
- Legal: review contractual constraints for enterprise contracts (Kiran to prefetch list).
- Engineering: confirm telemetry and safe rollback gates.
- Customer Success: draft proactive outreach and talking points for top 50 impacted customers.

Monitoring and measurement (KPIs):
- Token-weighted margin (daily)
content_continued:
- Churn delta (7/30/90 day windows) for accounts affected by uplift
- GPU-hour cost per 100M tokens
- Cache hit rate and latency P99 for affected routes
- Hiring velocity (SRE/infra) vs closure time

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How aggressive should we be on the burst-to-price mix for Q1 2027? (Ops view prefers burst; Finance prefers price-first.)
- Is there appetite for a pilot quota surcharge for new signups only?
- What is acceptable churn tolerance for top-customers (nominally 1.0–1.5% for moderate actions)?

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Finance: run Monte Carlo on churn vs uplift (Elena) — due 2026-11-20.
- Infra: estimate marginal cache uplift impact for two heavy customer routes (Miguel) — due 2026-11-17.
- Sales: list top 120 accounts by consumption and suggested uplift buckets (Kiran) — due 2026-11-19.
- Product: implement quick flag to enable surge-surcharge for small cohort (Sophie) — due 2026-11-25.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep playbook lightweight; this will live in Drive as the running source of truth during budget season.
- We should attach a simple sheet with scenario math (MonteCarlo outputs + token-to-GPU mapping) — tracked in linked_artifacts.

Appendix (short formulas):
- incremental_cost = GPU_hours_extra * spot_premium
- uplift_revenue = base_rev_segment * uplift_pct * retention_factor
- margin_delta_pp = (uplift_revenue - incremental_cost) / total_revenue_runrate * 100

End of doc.
